paragraph: Low-bit inference has moved arithmetic decisions that were once hidden inside well-understood floating-point libraries into handwritten or generated kernel code.  A four-bit quantity may be extracted into one byte lane, several lanes may then be multiplied together as a 32-bit word, and a bytewise intrinsic may repair a zero point without repairing a carry that crossed a lane boundary. Farther downstream, products can be narrowed, widened, wrapped, or saturated under a schedule chosen for throughput rather than for a simple source-level type.  Systems such as QServe motivate this combination of quantization and kernel co-design \cite{qserve}; recent optimized kernels continue to make arithmetic layout and overflow behavior a first-class design concern \cite{liquidgemm}.  The optimization opportunity is real, but so is the gap between a tensor-level formula and the finite-word program that implements it.
stated_citation_purpose: W4A8KV4 progressive quantization and register-level dequantization motivate the selected integer block.

paragraph: A conventional response is to ask a bit-vector solver whether the lowered fragment equals a reference fragment.  Solver-backed translation validation is powerful, and systems such as Alive2 demonstrate the value of a precise operational semantics and per-transformation checking \cite{alive2}.  For the kernel idioms studied here, however, the explicit arithmetic structure exposes two useful facts.  First, the packed decoder has a much simpler exact characterization: under the actual nibble/byte parameter bound, its carry is smaller than one byte, and a monotone upper-envelope recurrence decides universal safety in linear time.  Second, the accumulator is not well served by either of the two rules commonly used in engineering discussions.  Requiring every prefix to fit is sound but can reject final-only computations that reconverge after saturation.  Checking only the final exact range is not sound because an earlier saturation or term narrowing may have irreversibly changed the value. An exact analysis must retain enough history to distinguish these cases while remaining small enough to replay independently.
stated_citation_purpose: Bounded LLVM refinement validation, including undefined behavior; not an evaluated baseline here.

PICO optimizes Presburger in-bounds checks for memory-safety instrumentation \cite{pico}; interleaved SIMD vectorization changes data and instruction organization \cite{interleaved-vectorization}. Visual polyhedral editing exposes loop transformations \cite{visual-polyhedral}, and automatic GPU code generation from polyhedral representations changes schedules and execution placement \cite{ppcg}. The next-700-accelerated-layers work translates computation-graph expressions into GPU kernels \cite{next700}. Our fixed finite schedule does not verify those schedule or placement transformations.
stated_citation_purpose: Interactive polyhedral transformation and visualization; no human-study evidence is inherited.

paragraph: Packed arithmetic predates quantized serving. Lamport describes processing multiple bytes with full-word instructions \cite{lamport}; Fisher and Dietz study subword parallelism \cite{fisherdietz}; \emph{Hacker's Delight} collects low-level arithmetic constructions \cite{hackersdelight}. Packing small integers into general-purpose registers is directly related representation work \cite{packing}. Fixed-point conversion addresses finite-precision representation changes \cite{fixedpoint-conversion}; fixed-point arithmetic in residue number systems uses another numerical representation \cite{fixedpoint-rns}. Packed carries and finite-precision conversion are established phenomena in these antecedents.
stated_citation_purpose: Historical packed full-word arithmetic and masking.

stated_citation_purpose: Overflow can be intentional or erroneous; the cited journal expansion is distinguished from ICSE 2012.
